author: Times News
description:
“It’s [a conversation] we have avoided, and by avoiding it, we’ve got ourselves into what I regard as a much worse position.”

There needs to be more dialogue with the British public around the prisons system. It is important that sentences are carried out and are not changed halfway through, as it “undermines public confidence”, says judge and former Lord Chief Justice of England and Wales, Lord John Thomas.

Lord John Thomas was speaking to Nick Wallis on Times Radio Weekend Drive. Listen live from 4-7pm every Saturday and Sunday.

“If we don’t do this, Labour can forget the idea of building 1.5 million homes.”

description:
“Ossoff is the problem. Everything was moving along well for him, then he deviated from script.”

Jon Ossoff, who is seeking re-election in Georgia, should have “won without a problem”, but his jibe at longtime White House aide Natalie Harp will make him look “dumb”, says Democratic strategist and media consultant Hank Sheinkopf. 

Hank Sheinkopf and Marc Lotter were speaking to Ryan Tubridy on Times Radio. Listen live every Sunday, 1–4pm.

“This wasn’t just about trade and tariff levels, it really was about whether we could control the conditions of our sovereignty.”

author: Times News
description:
Karen Carter was murdered outside her home in the tranquil Dordogne village of Trémolat. The police launched a manhunt, and slowly a story of obsession, romance, and unrequited love started to come to light. So, why would someone murder a well-liked member of the community? And what’s the latest development in the police investigation?
